edits.section: Header 'Status' (lines 3-5) and §1 'Where the experts' mappings overrule' (lines 29-41)
edits.edit: Line 3: replace 'It replaces the rules of version 1 and its three amendments' with 'It replaces the rules of version 1 and of amendments 2 and 3. Amendment 1 stays in force on the owner's word for F1 (where the review runs), F2 (the form of a second expert) and the research child's 300k ceiling until he rules (§12).' Bullet at lines 32-33: delete 'and the coordinator' from the trusted-only readers and add: 'The coordinator is labelled low: the harness puts each child's 400-character note into its window. That is harmless because the coordinator certifies nothing. Every procedure it invokes checks its own inputs (Clark-Wilson).' Bullet at lines 36-38: replace it with 'The B+ tree governs what must share one window: the pack at review. The square-root law (R51) governs the coordinator and the fresh-review path. How long the research child's window runs is the owner's decision (§12).' Bullet at lines 39-41: replace 'coverage is an upper bound (D6-04)' with 'coverage is held-out seed recall (D8-10)', and replace 'the completeness estimate is a stop signal' with 'the completeness estimate is a reading, never a stop or a gate'.
edits.why: Version 2 decides F1 three ways while §12 still calls it his: by its default, by the role table and by R51's window. It also decides F2 and the child's ceiling, which amendment 1 records as his word and amendment 3 E.3 refused to reverse. The coordinator receives notes it did not request, so it cannot be a trusted-only reader. Rule 5 of this ruling: only the options and the default may be made clearer.

edits.edit: Row 1: replace 'escrow admission' with 'admission by a computed reservation'. Row 3: delete '(LCF kernel)' and 'Gordon, Milner and Wadsworth 1979'. §4 lines 191-192: replace 'the checker is an LCF-style kernel that alone promotes an item (D7-01)' with 'promote.mjs is the only writer of store/status/ (R14), behind the harness deny rules of R30. Only witnessed is certified by a script (result checking, D7-01). Confirmed is a judgment whose detection rate is measured (R43).' Row 6: keep the name 'B+ tree bulk-loaded at a fill factor' and add one sentence to §7's 'where assumptions fail': 'At seven leaves the borrowed parts are node capacity, fill factor, splitting the key range with a separator written to the parent, and never dropping a key. Height, search, latches and merges add nothing.'
edits.why: LCF's guarantee needs a theorem type that only kernel rules can build. Here any writer of store/status/ can produce 'confirmed', and promote writes it from a model's verdict, so the name claims a guarantee the design lacks. Escrow needs atomic debit against the reservation, which nothing here does. The B+ tree name stays because its split and never-drop rules are really used once R49(d) writes a separator. What is not borrowed is said once.

edits.edit: Move the run root out of every repository and out of every folder that has a CLAUDE.md or a .claude/ above it, for example C:/research-runs/2026-11-harness-leads/, kept in its own git repository with no CLAUDE.md. The design documents stay in harness-engineering. Change run/ to: tasks.json, ledger.jsonl, status.json, coord.json (ce, session, acked_seq, alarm pid), watcher.json (per-task call and tick counters), watcher.lock, run.lock, intents/ (messages to the owner only). R23: take the lean baseline from a control session started in an empty folder outside every repository. Every manifest names the user-level files that still load (the user CLAUDE.md, the user settings), by hash, as a declared input. Change 'clean' (R28) to 'reads only manifest inputs, the named user-level files included'.
edits.why: Attempt folders inside the harness-engineering repository load its CLAUDE.md files, and those carry earlier verdicts and hopes, which is the owner's anchoring problem. The transcript never shows these as reads, so neither R23 nor R28 can see them. A hermetic folder removes the channel instead of auditing it (D7-04, Shake).

edits.edit: Replace R1's text with: 'One lock, run/run.lock, covers every shared write: tasks.json, a ledger append (the tail is read inside the lock), status.json and the git commit. It is created with wx and holds {pid, process start time, nonce}. A busy lock gets a short bounded retry, then exit 75. A stale lock is broken only by renaming it to a unique name and checking that the renamed file still holds the pid, start time and nonce judged stale; on a mismatch it is renamed back. Every --ce and epoch check happens inside the lock. Temp files are named <file>.<pid>.<nonce>.tmp, then renamed. Unparseable table: as now.' Basis: D3-10, D2-05, model extra flaw E1.
edits.why: lib.mjs runs inside several processes at once: the watcher's intake and the scripts the coordinator calls, possibly as parallel tool calls in one turn. So the ledger chain can fork and git's index lock collides. The stale-lock break was check-then-act, which can produce two writers and silently undo a fence. Version 2 states no break at all, so a crashed holder blocks everything forever.

edits.edit: Add: 'The fence is a compare-and-set under the run lock: replace.mjs passes the target epoch, and the epoch becomes e+1 (restarts +1 for a failure reason) only if it is still e. At the fence the task row records the attempt's staging cut: per staging file, its byte length and the sha256 of that prefix (log truncation at the leader epoch, as in Kafka; an extension of D1-01). The coordinator always passes the table's epoch to commit.mjs. A READY in a stale attempt folder is logged only as zombie-write telemetry. Every script that writes takes --ce.' Basis: D1-01, D3-09.
edits.why: Redoing the fence is not idempotent: a coordinator crash in mid-replace would raise the epoch again and charge a second restart, which under R = 1 parks a healthy task. The staging cut is what R8 needs to stop post-fence output from entering the next attempt. Several scripts (intent, status, salvage) had no ce or epoch check.

edits.edit: Replace R3 with: 'R3. Start and replace are a step machine in the task row (pilot): fenced, stop-requested, stopped, admitted, started(session id), bound. Each script call names the target epoch and the step it expects, and acts only if the row is there. The coordinator performs only the session-tool step that the row names. status.mjs --reconcile runs at the start of every coordinator turn: a transcript on disk for the attempt folder means the start happened, so it is recorded. Commit records and pack freezes are idempotent by exclusive create. Only a message to the owner keeps an intent file. A refused admission leaves the row at its step, with no new fence and no new count.' Basis: D1-07, D1-12, D3-09.
edits.why: An intent redone from step 1 re-fences and re-counts. Reconcile ran only at coordinator start, so a torn step inside a live coordinator waited forever. The row itself can be the intent log. That deletes the intent files for start, replace, commit and freeze (state that can be derived is not stored), and settles model A7, where a task was stranded after the fence.

edits.edit: Replace with: 'R4. The watcher (pilot). watch.mjs reads, decides and exits. It holds run/watcher.lock (wx; pid, process start time, ce) for its whole life. The ce check is the first act of every tick and is repeated inside the lock before each append. Intake (harvest, commit, snap, witness, tms, status) runs as a separate process that the watcher spawns and does not wait for, one at a time under the run lock. Its results are read at the next tick. Spend is computed in the tick by lib's single transcript parser. The watcher exits at once on an urgent event (stall, hang, loop, hard limit, memory, failed stop) and within δ on others. It also exits on a newer ce. A checker batch is an event only when it is full or when it is the only thing blocking a task. There is no deadline exit.' Basis: D3-06, D3-07, IEC 61508-7 (a watchdog is independent of what it watches).
edits.why: Model flaw F4: endturn's undefined 'fresh tick' let two watchers append. Intake inside the tick let a slow fetch or a large commit pass for sleep (A2-07), and a hung fetch silences the only event source. The T_watch deadline exit woke the coordinator when nothing had changed. That is polling at full-window price (about 137k tokens per call by cost.js), which is the cost G6 says the watcher exists to avoid. Checker batches each cost a wake of their own.

edits.edit: R5: replace 'Stall: no fall in V and no new primary on an uncovered id for T_box' with 'Stall: c consecutive model calls across the attempt's transcripts with no fall in V. Hang: h watcher ticks with no new call in any transcript of the attempt. Both counters are kept per task in run/watcher.json and continued by any later watcher. A tick counts at most once per Δ. No clock reads elapsed wall time. A READY of the current epoch voids any suspicion of that epoch.' c and h are guesses until the pilot measures them (§11 replaces T_box with c and h). Delete R6 and its §9 row N2 rule (replaced by R5's counters).
edits.why: Model flaw F3: pause detection lived only inside one live watcher's consecutive ticks, so the next watcher suspected healthy attempts and charged their only restart. A sleeping PC makes no calls and no ticks, so counters in those units cannot mistake sleep for a stall, which deletes the pause bookkeeping. Persisting the counters is the model's FIX_CLOCK, and it avoids the reviewer's caveat (a clock reset at each watcher never fires). The rule that READY voids suspicion settles model A4 and the reviewer's recoverable-stall finding.

edits.edit: Replace the endturn clause with: 'status.mjs --endturn makes sure two wake sources that the coordinator itself started are pending: the watcher, and an alarm (watch.mjs --alarm, a long sleep and then an exit). Each endturn kills and re-arms the alarm, so it fires only after a long silence. Its pid and ce go in coord.json. Endturn writes acked_seq into coord.json under the run lock, and exits 1 unless both sources run. A coordinator woken with a stale ce ends its turn without running any script that writes. The bound is restated in R7, §9 N3 and R58: a wake arrives while either source lives; if both wakes are lost, only the owner wakes the tree.' The pilot injects one lost wake (R43's fault list).
edits.why: Model flaw F2: after the watcher's own urgent exit, a lost wake was permanent (NoDeadlock fails in 5 steps). Under harness fact 2, only the exit of a background command the session started can start its turn, so a second self-started command is the only redundancy with a runner. No file held the acknowledged seq, so one-shot events were acted on twice or missed after a hand-over.

edits.edit: R8: replace 'checkpoint = last commit record plus the dead attempt's schema-valid objects' with 'checkpoint = the commit records plus the dead attempt's staging prefixes at or below the cut recorded at the fence (R2). Those objects enter the new attempt's in/ as untrusted staging and pass commit.mjs again. For a failure reason, replace.mjs first re-checks under the run lock for a READY of the current epoch, and if it finds one it refuses with its own exit code, so the commit wins.' Line 128: replace with 'one commit per task holds because consumers read commit records and the restart path reads only the prefix cut at the fence.' Add to the paragraph: 'Suspicion is not final: a slow call recovers, so READY outranks suspicion. A stop may not take effect, so slots count live processes. A host reset is a common cause, not a task failure. A session cannot be woken by a timer it did not start.'
edits.why: Model flaw F1: NoStaleAccepted fails with every mechanism present, and a planned hand-over alone is enough. R8 was a second consumer that read uncommitted output, which contradicted R15 and line 128. The reviewer showed that a READY landing during a coordinator turn is replaced and charged as a restart.
rests_on: model extra: READY during a turn

edits.edit: Replace with: 'A failed task is replaced at most once (R = 1, any class). A restart is class host, with no charge to R and no count toward W_cc, when the OS boot time (from os.uptime) is later than the attempt's start. On the limit path, replace.mjs fences, runs stop.mjs and only then marks the task failed for the owner. Its slot is freed when the stop is confirmed; until then it counts as live (R11). Memory parking counts toward H_max.' Basis: D1-09, D4-07 (beta factor: a common cause is split from independent failures).
edits.why: Model flaw F5: escalation left the failed attempt running and spending. Its spend was never zombie spend, because the attempt was never fenced. A reboot kills every child at once, and this PC has a recorded history of hard resets, so charging it would spend every task's only restart. Model A1: the same-class rule made R vacuous, and with R = 1 over any class it is no longer needed. Model A8: parking had no cap.

edits.edit: Replace the admission conditions with: 'Fewer than N_max live child processes, stop-unconfirmed ones included (2 until memory is measured, never above 3). A reservation computed at each admission and never stored: Σ measured spend of every attempt (zombie and post-limit spend included) + Σ (e_task − spent) over admitted and running tasks; admit if B − reservation − r ≥ e_new. The gate is bound to the hash of the design cut (R56). Design-check tasks (blind analyses, mapper, canary helpers) take slots, reservation and fencing, but not the gate. Before a review task, gate A: every approved id is covered by a witnessed or confirmed card or listed as not covered, and the share of unverifiable cards is under its line.' Rename escrow to 'admission reservation' throughout. State that B is a target the owner enforces beyond r, not a bound.
edits.why: Model flaw F6: admission counted table rows, so a zombie plus its replacement exceeded the cap. Slots fails at the interim N = 2, and at N = 3 with 4 events. The stored escrow leaked on failed, parked and replaced tasks until admission starved. The gate needed sessions that themselves needed the gate. A review could start on a pack that was barely covered, so the 'raw opinion' the owner set out to avoid was caught only after its tokens were spent (amendment 1 point 3: checked, then it reviews).

edits.edit: Retitle R12 'Spend measured by script, stopped by the coordinator'. The watcher's tick decides, exits urgent, and the coordinator stops the child. Delete the 20 % meter halt. The coordinator logs meter readings as lines marked self-reported, compared only at the end of the pilot. Report the overshoot per incident, with no bound claimed. The cut writes an overflow record {ids, tokens, reason} to the ledger, and those ids stay visible as not covered in every view. R10: if a stop does not end the helpers, the owner ends the process, and its tokens are charged to B as zombie spend.
edits.why: Only a session stops a session (fact 1), and a script cannot read the meter (fact 6). So the 20 % check rested on a typed figure, against R32. The whole-percent meter also moves with the owner's other sessions. The overshoot term contains a wake latency that has no bound once a wake can be lost. The overflow record keeps paid-for ids visible (D2-02) until the split path exists.

edits.section: R13, R51 for the coordinator, and §12 'Coordinator hand-over' (lines 115-118, 354-358, 557-558)
edits.edit: R13: define the drain. From W*_coord the coordinator blocks every start (first starts, planned replacements and failure restarts). A child that reaches its limit commits and ends with no successor. Quiescence means no live child process of any epoch. The coordinator then asks the owner, and handover.mjs kills the watcher and the alarm and raises ce. At the 300k quality line with no answer from the owner, it ends its turns until he comes. R51: delete 'stops at 1.5·W*' for the coordinator; audit.mjs flags every coordinator turn above 1.5·W*_coord to the owner. §9 G8 remains: 'obedience; only the owner can stop the coordinator'. §12 'Coordinator hand-over': list the options. (a) The drain above: the silent default, as now. (b) Crash-only: fence every running child as a planned replacement (a supervisor restart restarts its subtree, D1-09, D1-12). It saves idle time, but each child pays a hand-over re-read and, under amendment 1, loses the field it holds. (c) The hand-over point: by token count W* = 133.2k (default), weighted W* = 157.1k, or a band up to the 200k line. By cost.js that is about 12 % more per call against about 2.3 times as many hand-overs (stand-in inputs). Add owner interventions per hour and the owner's start latency to §11.
edits.why: A quiet point that never comes is real only if draining lets replacements continue, which was left unspecified (model A3). Blocking every start makes the drain end within one child epoch. Quiescence by table state ignored zombies. Nothing can stop the coordinator but the owner, so the 1.5·W* stop and G8's 'None known' overstated. Under rule 5 the hand-over form stays his: the options and their prices are made explicit, and the default is unchanged.

edits.section: §4 R29, R30, R32 and the role table
edits.edit: R29: tcb.lock.json is no longer the reference. The owner's go message names the approved tcb commit hash, the coordinator's brief echoes it, every tcb-verify compares against it, and the owner page shows it so he can compare. Label it tamper-evident, not tamper-proof. R30: add permission deny rules in the user-level settings for Write and Edit on the run root's tcb/**, run/**, store/**, sealed/**, review-in/** and wt/*/.claude/**. They name only research paths, so the owner's other work is untouched. Per-folder settings keep Bash refused except the coordinator's `node tcb/scripts/*`. The R42 canary also tests these denies. audit.mjs exits 3 on any write call that touches tcb/, .claude/, sealed/ or review-in/. R32: delete 'as a chain gives forward integrity only'. Write instead: 'tamper-evident against writers who do not recompute the chain; a deliberate rewrite is caught only against a head the owner noted'. R14 and the role table: replace.mjs alone builds review-in/<task>/, from the frozen pack hash, the must-read snapshots and the field's fixed file list in protocol.json.
edits.why: Clark-Wilson, the reference monitor, Tripwire and Schneier-Kelsey all assume a principal or a key that the subjects cannot reach. Here every session runs as one Windows user, tcb.lock.json sits inside the folder it protects, and the chain has no key. The harness's own permission check is the cheapest enforcement point outside the per-folder files. A fresh reviewer's whole context had no named writer, so the coordinator's opinion could enter it.

edits.edit: R33: replace 'One harness-imposed card schema' with 'The harness validates a reader's result against the schema the child passes. harvest.mjs re-validates every result against tcb's card schema, so an altered schema costs only retries, and cards made that way count as copied_by_session.' Move R49(a), the budget check in the hook, to later. In the pilot the watcher logs the predicted against the realised t_q per group. Add to §13 that it is unknown whether a pre-call hook sees an Agent call's schema and the session's transcript path.
edits.why: The child imposes the schema (fact 3), so 'harness-imposed' meant obedience. A script re-check at harvest closes it without trusting hook inputs nobody has verified. R49(a) would gate on prior t_q values with inputs the hook may not receive.

edits.edit: Keep the manifest (brief, schema, tier, tools, input hashes, the named user-level files) as the reference for R23 and R28. Delete 'status.mjs reuses a result with that key and no STALE node, repairs only STALE nodes' and move keyed reuse to later. Recovery is R8, from commit records.
edits.why: Model steps are never rerun to verify them, and early cutoff applies to script steps only, which cost no model tokens. The reuse that does save tokens is resuming from commit records, which R8 already gives.

edits.section: R36, R57 and §8 'What the estimate says today'
edits.edit: R36: the coverage figure is held-out seed recall per field, with its Clopper-Pearson interval. Label it an upper bound for a stated reason (seeds are probably easier to find than the average relevant source), as an assumption. Chapman is computed pooled per field, only from routes that happened anyway, and only as a diagnostic of route dependence. Per-question two-route capture moves to later. R57: delete the threshold and the extra-lens rule. Chapman and Chao2 are readings that never pass, stop or add anything. The pilot's incident list (R59) is the next capture source, not another blind lens. §8 last sentence: replace 'so R55 runs before the pilot' with 'so the estimate is reported, not used as a stop'.
edits.why: Chapman is an upper bound only under positive dependence. R36 deliberately picks routes of different mechanism, which pulls the estimate the other way, and the completeness analysis calls its own direction unknown. Section 8 itself says no estimator is valid and every one exceeds the experts' stop of 2 or 3, so R57 either never passes or adds lenses without end. Per-question two-route capture roughly doubles reader searches to get a figure the document calls biased.

edits.edit: R44: delete the SPRT and the uncited-card lot (lot moves to later). Every cited card is checked, and certification requires each to be confirmed and to pass R19. The escape rate measured on seeds is reported beside the review. R43: one checker call carries at most one seed of each class, at a random position among real items, and the Clopper-Pearson bound counts calls, not seeds (14 calls at d0 = 0.8). R45: split into gate A (in admit.mjs, before the review: R11) and the certificate after the review (reads match the manifest, cited cards confirmed, plants found). R46 and §12 thresholds: silence on a threshold means the default stated in its mapping, logged as such (d0 = 0.8, β = 0.05). Where no mapping gives a default (plants t, coverage floor, action lines), the item is a reading in the pilot, not a gate.
edits.why: An SPRT over a fully inspected lot makes the verdict depend on order and restates 'every cited card is confirmed'. Its α and β ignore the checker's own detection rate. Uncited cards feed no trusted consumer (R25). Seeds judged in one window are not independent trials (pseudoreplication). One seed per class per call keeps the calibration at 14 calls instead of 112. Silence on any threshold stopped all admission.

edits.edit: R55: 'gate.mjs --cut' writes the design cut: the layout, the role table, the script lists and the rule texts, with §8, §9, §13, every 'where the classical assumptions fail' paragraph and every P, N, G, D and K id removed. The blind analysts get only the cut and run in hermetic folders (layout edit). audit.mjs refuses an analysis whose transcript read the full design. They run before the pilot, after it, and whenever the cut's hash changes. R56: the gate binds to the hash of the cut plus hazards.jsonl, not to tcb.lock.json. A tcb change reruns selftest and the canary only. Remove R57 from the gate. R58: the protocol model is the existing tree-v2/model/model.mjs, extended. It models the adopted designs, not oracles: the alarm, the call and tick counters, the watcher lock, the compare-and-set step machine with a coordinator crash, the lock break and live-process counting. Its properties are strengthened: COMMIT creations are counted; Slots and FailedTaskStopped count live processes; R = 1; a 4-event budget, with the budget checked when a plan runs, not when it is built; recoverable stalls; READY landing during a turn. Record the current verdict: blocked, until the extended model holds.
edits.why: R55 gave the 'blind' analysts the very risk list it says to withhold, which inflates the overlap and biases the residual low. Binding the gate to tcb.lock.json made every one-line script fix call for new blind sessions. R58's own rule blocks version 2: the model found six flaws with every mechanism present, and the review showed that AtMostOneCommit, Slots, RestartLimit and FailedTaskStopped were vacuous or weak, the budget was overspent, and FIX_REWAKE and FIX_CLOCK were oracles.

edits.edit: Add to R21: render.mjs computes the owner's seven measures per task, field and arm from the transcripts and the ledger. Throughput: approved ids covered by a witnessed or confirmed card, per hour. Efficiency: confirmed answers per million tokens. Token count: all transcripts, helpers included. Token cost: the count weighted by the provider's relative prices per tier and cache class, with no currency. Time taken: from ledger timestamps, with sleep gaps shown apart. Quality: Comparison 1's primary plus the blinded rubric. Hallucinations: witness rejections, checker rejections, citation failures and the seeded escape rate. They go on the owner page. R46's action lines and Comparison 1's secondaries are stated in these seven. Add coordinator calls and tokens per field, and owner interventions per hour, as §11 parameters.
edits.why: The owner judges everything by these seven, yet version 2 names none of them and no script computes them. Version 1's ledger rule that reported them was dropped. Coordinator wakes are the main uncounted token term (about 137k tokens each at k* by cost.js, on stand-in inputs).

edits.edit: Comparison 1: S1 runs with no fan-out until the 300k quality line, then stops. It is not compacted or handed over, and its uncovered ids are counted. R54 and F4 state the pilot's predicted total over every arm (T, R_same, R1, R2, S1, and S2 if allowed), using cost.js figures marked stand-in. Comparison 2: the pilot child runs in amendment 1's form (one session up to the ceiling), so that R_same really holds the field. Delete 'judgment share' as a secondary. Add D8-07's count of factual sentences in R_same that cite nothing in the frozen pack. Keep R2 unconditionally, as part of the frozen plan. State that the D6-10 crossed design (a review of pack B from an independent research run) is an F2 option, off unless the owner allows its cost of about one more research run.
edits.why: The comparisons cost about one or two fields more, and that was stated nowhere. S1's behaviour at the cap (cross, compact or stop) changes what P18 measures. A same-window review under W* roll-overs would hold only the last epoch, so Comparison 2 needs amendment 1's form to measure F1 at all. Judgment share penalises the same-window arm by construction (line 184).

edits.section: §12 F1, F2, a new item 'Research child's window', and the hook item
edits.edit: F1: the silent default is amendment 1: the child that researched reviews in the same session, and a fresh session reviews past the 300k ceiling. The fresh-from-pack path also runs at least once per wave (D4-08, D1-12). The pilot writes both reviews (Comparison 2) and he rules after it. Delete 'no difference shown defaults to fresh'. Add a 'child (reviewing)' row to the role table, marked 'under F1 option a'. F2: silent default is no second expert until he rules. If he wants one, the options are amendment 1's form (a second child researching independently) or the mapper's form (a second reviewer of the same pack plus the contrary-evidence reader), and the D6-10 crossed design can measure the difference at the cost of one research run. New item 'Research child's window': (a) amendment 1: one session up to the 300k ceiling, then freeze; the ids left over go to an overflow record and later to a split (silent default, his word). (b) Roll-overs at W* (R50, R51) and a fresh review: by cost.js about 2.4 to 4.4 times fewer tokens than one unbounded session (stand-in inputs), with a quality loss no formula prices. The hand-over measure gains 'quality' as a third option. Hook item: state the reach of each option. Per-folder rules sit inside a folder the coordinator's Write can reach. User-level research-path denies (R30) apply in the pilot either way. The Windows-account fallback stays his.
edits.why: These are recorded as his decisions. Version 2 resolved them by default, by the role table and by R51. The edit restores his recorded word as the silent default and puts the trade, with its token figures, in front of him.

edits.edit: R48: in the pilot the leaves are the lanes, with one capacity check at pack freeze (C_node = W_quality − P − R_rev; no confirmed card is cut). plan-tree.mjs runs after the pilot on the t_q measured by unit-costs, before wave 1. A lane over f·C splits by group range then, before any spend. An id with no estimate is listed and blocks admission (D2-01 on_failure). R49: (a) and (c) move to later. (d) becomes a split: the overflow record becomes a new leaf whose separator is written into tree-plan.json, and the field's review reads both leaves through R18's two-level index (later). gate.mjs refuses the synthesis while any range is neither committed, scheduled, nor dropped on the owner's quoted word (later, before the first synthesis). R50 applies only under option (b) of the research child's window.
edits.why: Bulk loading packs entries of known size, but t_q and κ_q are unmeasured and R48 itself says 'on priors'. One pilot field needs no inner level (root fan-out of 246 by cost.js). A split that does not update the parent is ISAM overflow chaining, not a B+ split.

edits.edit: P8 remains: 'helpers bounded by the reservation only'. P9 rules: R4, R5, R7, R10; remains: 'both wake sources lost: only the owner wakes the tree; PC awake unproven'. P10 remains: add 'host resets are not charged'. P11 remains: 'owner starts the successor; the drain idles slots'. P12 remains: 'overshoot reported per incident; no bound after a lost wake'. N2: rule R5 (counters in calls and ticks). N3: rules R7 (watcher + alarm), R13, R58; remains: 'both wakes lost'. N5 remains: 'a torn step is retried by reconcile at each turn'. N9 remains: 'the model check found no slot deadlock within its bounds; the lost-wake deadlock is fixed in R7'. N16 remains: 'tamper-evident against the owner's noted head only'. G8 remains: 'obedience; only the owner can stop the coordinator'. P13: replace 'SPRT' with 'gate A, certificate'.
edits.why: Several rows claim that residuals were closed when the model had already refuted them, or name mechanisms that the edits above delete.

edits.edit: Add: each child session is a separate OS process that a script can find and kill by its folder; a process's start time can be read (through PowerShell) to guard against PID reuse; a background command's exit starts a turn even when it fires during a turn, during sleep, or after ce changed; user-level permission denies bind every session and cannot be bypassed through `node`; which settings files apply to a session started in an attempt folder; whether a pre-call hook sees an Agent call's schema and transcript path. Each gets a probe in the pilot's fault list (R43) and a stated fallback: the owner ends the process, and the tokens are counted as zombie spend.
edits.why: R10, R11, the alarm in R7 and the deny rules in R30 all rest on these facts, and none of them was on the list.

edits.why: Almost every flaw the model found came from a mechanism added to coordinate other mechanisms. Removing and merging shrinks the pilot to what the problems rated high, and the six model flaws, require.

pilot_set_final: Scripts (Node 24, in tcb/, each with fixtures), 25 in all:
lib.mjs: the run lock with a verified stale break, unique temp names, ledger append with the tail read in the lock, the compare-and-set fence, the single transcript parser.
admit.mjs: counts live processes, computes the reservation, gate A before reviews, admits design-check tasks.

replace.mjs: the step machine in the task row, the staging cut at the fence, restore of the cut prefix, a READY re-check under the lock, the host class, fence and stop before 'failed'; it builds attempt folders and their settings (absorbs make-profile) and builds review-in/.
stop.mjs.
watch.mjs: reads, decides and exits; watcher.lock; call and tick counters; spawns intake without waiting; computes spend; --alarm mode.
status.mjs: --reconcile every turn; --endturn checks that the watcher and the alarm run and writes acked_seq.
handover.mjs: kills the watcher and the alarm, raises ce.
harvest.mjs: re-validates against tcb's card schema.
commit.mjs.
tms.mjs: labels, including the dismissal bar of R39.
render.mjs: views, the coverage view (held-out seed recall), the seven measures.
audit.mjs: reads, writes into protected paths (exit 3), search log, notes, coordinator turns above 1.5·W*.
fsck.mjs: absorbs tcb-verify against the commit the owner named.
guard-hook.mjs.
snap.mjs and witness.mjs: need F5; without it every card is unverifiable and the pilot only measures.
check-queue.mjs and promote.mjs.
protocol-freeze.mjs, with the held-out seed split.
compare.mjs.
selftest.mjs: includes the canary for hooks and user-level denies.
seed.mjs: one seed per class per checker call.
certify.mjs.
cost.mjs (the existing cost.js) with a --from-transcripts mode for unit costs at the pilot's end.
gate.mjs: --cut for the design cut.
protocol-model.mjs (the existing model.mjs), extended per the R58 edit and passing.

not_established: Whether a background command's exit starts the coordinator's turn when it fires during a turn, during sleep, or after ce changed. The alarm design and the lost-wake bound rest on it.
Whether user-level permission denies bind every session started in another folder, and whether `node` run through Bash can get around them.
Whether child sessions are separate OS processes that a script can find by folder, and whether a process's start time can be read reliably to guard against PID reuse.
Whether hooks fire for helpers, and whether a pre-call hook sees an Agent call's schema and transcript path.
Whether a background script, or intake spawned without waiting, keeps the PC awake; and how Node's interval timers behave after sleep on Windows (the counters assume at most one count per Δ).
Whether the extended model holds once the adopted fixes are modelled as designs rather than oracles. It has not run, so version 2 is blocked by its own R58.
The pilot's total token cost with every arm. Only cost.js figures on stand-in inputs exist.
Coordinator calls per wake and wakes per field; the owner's start latency; owner interventions per hour.
Whether amendment 1's single research session to 300k or W* roll-overs give better reviews. No source compares them for this job, and the pilot gives n = 1 per arm.
Whether held-out seed recall overstates coverage. Its direction rests on the assumption that seeds are easier to find than the average relevant source.
Whether the coordinator could start its own successor without the old session's wakes costing full-window calls.
